old_caption: The video captures a simple yet dynamic scene featuring a pink ball in motion against a minimalist backdrop. Initially, the ball is seen in mid-air, descending towards a flat surface. As it approaches the ground, the ball bounces multiple times before settling on the surface. The background is a plain white wall, which provides a stark contrast to the vibrant pink color of the ball. The surface on which the ball lands appears to be a light-colored, flat board on a wooden floor. The lighting is well-lit with a bright background. There are no other objects or characters present in the scene, focusing all attention on the ball's trajectory and its interaction with the surface.

Initially, the ball is seen in mid-air, descending towards a flat surface. As it approaches the ground, the ball bounces once before coming to rest on the surface. The background is a plain white wall, which provides a stark contrast to the vibrant pink color of the ball. The surface on which the ball lands appears to be a wooden table or platform, adding a subtle texture to the otherwise smooth setting. The lighting is even and bright, highlighting the ball's movement and the clean lines of the environment. There are no other objects or characters present in the scene, focusing all attention on the ball's trajectory and its interaction with the surface. The video ends with the ball stationary on the wooden surface, completing the sequence of its fall and bounce.
caption: The video captures a single pink ball suspended in front of a plain off-white wall, hovering above a light wooden mat. The ball is already in motion on the first frame, drifting downward from an elevated position toward the surface. As it nears the mat, a soft shadow appears beneath it, tracking its descent. Around the middle of the excerpt the ball meets the mat and flattens into a wide squash shape before springing back to a round form and lifting just above the surface. For a long stretch it hangs at a low, nearly steady height, with the shadow fading and reappearing as its distance from the mat changes. The ball then settles back down to a second contact, squashing flat once more. After rebounding to a round silhouette it rises only slightly, ending the clip hovering a short distance above the mat. Throughout, the wall and mat remain still, so the visible motion belongs entirely to the bouncing ball.
